## Detailed Instructions:

**Step 1: Read the Structure of an Execution Session**
When opening the Log stream, you will see a series of text lines. A successful Lambda execution session will always have the following required structure:
* `START RequestId: ...` (Starts receiving the event from S3).
* Log lines generated by the Python code (if there are errors, details will be printed in red in this area).
* `END RequestId: ...` (Ends processing).
* `REPORT RequestId: ...` (Summary report of system metrics).

**Step 2: Analyze the REPORT Line (Proof of Optimization)**
Focus on the line starting with `REPORT` and analyze the following 2 extremely important metrics:

1. **Duration (Execution time):**
   * *Evaluation:* This time is much lower than the 15.00-second Timeout limit we set in the Lambda configuration. This means the system runs safely without being forcibly cut short halfway through.

   ![alt text](/Workshop/images/4/4.9/image3.png)

2. **Max Memory Used:**
   * *Evaluation:* Lambda only allows 128 MB by default. If we had not proactively increased the Memory Size to 512 MB in the previous chapter, this function would definitely have crashed due to a RAM overflow since the Pillow library consumes quite a lot of memory for image compression.

   ![alt text](/Workshop/images/4/4.9/image4.png)
